label: early original-phase step reading 2/n/0/h/w/i/l/u/g after a sequence starting with r/3/c/f/d/t
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98% of mass), never at t=0 or 1, and peaks at t=3-4. It looks like a graded conjunction of two things: the current input is one of a few tokens (2 strongest at 7.8x lift, then n, 0, h, w, i, l, u, g), and the earlier prefix holds tokens from another set (r most of all, then 3, c, f, d, t), especially as the first token. Activations are largest when both hold and the prefix has several r/c/3 tokens (e.g. r r r [2], c c r r 3 [2]). Mostly fires on the first occurrence of the input token. Almost silent at the delimiter and in the copy phase. The behaviour looks additive and diffuse, so boolean predicates top out near F1 0.4. The broad version (any I-token at t>=2 in the original phase) covers 93% of activation mass but has only 8% precision.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=2: 2, n, 0, h; t=3: 2, n, 0, h; t=4: 2, n, 0, h) and the first original token (most: r, 3, c, f, d, t; least: i, q, 1, 2); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=11, L=9 & t=10.
